title: rust-cargo/typescript-npm: generate protocols + contexts and real-signature lib stubs (parity with python-uv)
description: Follow-up from dizzy-e4a2 (lib/-only migration). python-uv element packages now carry real-signature implementation stubs (derived from gen_int Protocols/contexts) and depend on the gen_def/gen_int packages. The rust-cargo and typescript-npm lib generators still emit degenerate stubs (rust: 'pub fn <name>() { todo!() }'; ts equivalent) because those runtimes generate only gen_def types under lib/<runtime>/gen_def — they have no protocol/context generation. Scope: generate gen_int-equivalent protocol/context types for rust/ts, then emit element stubs with real signatures (command/event/input/context/output) matching the protocol, and make each element package depend on the runtime's generated types. Until then, rust/ts remain experimental and their stubs are signature-less.

## Roleplay learnings (dizzy-0504 — sim/ manual dry-run, runs 1-3)

Scheduler-core rules validated by hand against sim/library.feat.yaml (sources: sim/PLAYBOOK.md ground rules; session sim/sessions/*.jsonl):
- PHASED LOOP (rule 1): drain the event queue (policies + projections) then the command queue (procedures), repeat. One legal interleaving; make no concurrency claims.
- TERMINATION (rule 5): default step budget 30. Repetition/livelock: same component activated on the same message shape 3x -> stop and record a possible-livelock finding. N configurable.
- INJECTION (ruling, run 1): inject ONE scenario command at a time; run to quiescence before the next.
- FIRST-EXECUTION REVIEW GATE (rule 11, born run 3 at t37): before activating a component whose execution count is 0 (a simple count gathered from the session log / event store), the scheduler PAUSES for human/Director review of its description. An unexecuted description may be partly/entirely wrong, and pre-first-execution is the one moment to fix it before breaking facts accumulate. Confirmed -> proceed; amended -> the feat revision applies from that node. The scheduler needs an execution-count hook and a pause/resume seam for this.
- LEVEL-0 PROJECTION SKIP (rule 10, jmQ collapse): at level 0 projections never activate and are never logged; the scheduler drains only events that have policy/querier consequences. Projection activation returns at level 2 (see dizzy-01cc).

## Roleplay learnings (dizzy-0504 — sim/ manual dry-run, runs 1-3)

Harness-contract rules validated by hand (sim/PLAYBOOK.md; sessions):
- TOOLS FROM WIRING ONLY (rule 2): synthesize exactly emit_<event> per declared emit, dispatch_<command> per policy emit, query_<name> per declared query. No tool, no emission. Observed sets: lend_book -> [query_get_member_registration, query_get_book_availability, query_get_next_reservation, emit_book_borrowed, emit_borrow_rejected, report_finding]; policy fulfill_reservation_on_return -> [query_get_next_reservation, dispatch_hold_copy_for_member, dispatch_notify_member, report_finding].
- report_finding ALWAYS present (rule 3).
- POLICIES MAY DECLARE QUERIES (dizzy-c9c5, shipped): tool synthesis must emit query_<name> tools for POLICY activations, not just procedures. The t37 trap (a policy needing reservation data with no way to query) is what drove c9c5; the contract now covers policy queries.
- NON-AUTONOMOUS-COMMAND-DISPATCH (finding u2, run 3): a policy may only dispatch commands the system can execute ITSELF. The original policy dispatched borrow_book, but borrowing is a physical human act — not dispatchable. Candidate semantic check at the contract/validation layer: flag policy emits whose command requires external/human action. Ties to dizzy-c5a0.
- Payload validation: at level 0 narrative only (no schema); rejection/re-prompt behavior begins at level >= 1.

## Roleplay learnings (dizzy-0504 — sim/ manual dry-run, runs 1-3)

Findings-pipeline rules validated by hand (sim/PLAYBOOK.md; sessions):
- PAUSE ON report_finding (rule 6): every finding checkpoints to the human/Director before the activation proceeds — never build on a wrong assumption.
- NO SPECULATIVE EMITS (rule 7): an activation that cannot logically deduce an outcome ends WITHOUT emitting. Emitting alongside a finding is allowed only for branches that ARE deducible.
- A FINDING ENDS AN ACTIVATION, NOT THE RUN (rule 8): the run continues to quiescence/budget collecting the full findings list (the product). Fixes happen at RUN END, then a branch from the pre-fix node verifies them under the amended feature-file.
- RECORD, DON'T SUGGEST (rule 9): every finding gets a resolution carrying the Director's decision AND the argument_as_stated VERBATIM (load-bearing: it encodes assumptions the design team cannot infer and may later prove wrong). The engine never editorializes, infers motives, or fills in punchlines.
- RESOLUTION CATEGORIES observed: design-change (feature-file wrong -> amend, branch, verify); insufficient-context (design fine, world under-specified -> amend scenario context, close branch, fork fresh); unreviewed-component (never executed, no evidence of correctness -> backtrack to pre-activation, rewrite description, re-attempt under rule 11).
- FINDING KINDS observed: missing-slot, ambiguous-description, undecidable-branch, unanswerable-query, missing-query-wiring (now resolved by dizzy-c9c5), non-autonomous-command-dispatch (u2), possible-livelock (rule 5).
- LIVELOCK DETECTOR (rule 5): same component + same message shape, N=3 -> possible-livelock finding rather than hard abort.

## Roleplay learnings (dizzy-0504 — sim/ manual dry-run, runs 1-3)

The --manual turn contract, exercised by hand (sim/PLAYBOOK.md 'Turn protocol'):
Each activation is one exchange:
  HARNESS -> component:
    component: <name> (<kind>)
    description: <verbatim from feat-file>
    trigger: <message type + payload narrative>
    tools: [<synthesized tool names> + report_finding]
  COMPONENT -> harness (JSON, one or more calls):
    {"tool": "query_...", "args": {...narrative...}}
    {"tool": "emit_..."/"dispatch_...", "args": {...narrative...}}
The harness validates every call (declared tool? plausible shape?), appends to the session log, and schedules consequences.
- QUERY ANSWERING (Q1 + rule 10, jmQ collapse): a query is answered by a synchronous SUB-ACTIVATION — a querier given the query's description and full read access to the simulated event store, answering from the stream (a dj-style regression). If the stream cannot answer -> report_finding. Queriers do not fabricate.
- LEVEL 0 = narrative payloads (prose), no schemas. First end-to-end target is guestbook; the library feat was the by-hand reference.
- The same message protocol is reused unchanged by --exec (dizzy-7259) and --provider (dizzy-1196).

title: simulate session file: versioned append-only JSONL run log (itself a DIZZY event stream) + deterministic replay
description:
Plan pl-f395 step 5. Requirements: docs/cli.md § dizzy simulate (session file paragraph). Versioned append-only JSONL whose entries carry id/parentId so the file is a tree (prior art: pi agent session format — branching is in-place appending to an earlier parent, context rebuild walks leaf->root). Entry-type vocabulary seeded by the sim/ roleplay (PLAYBOOK.md Q5). Scheduler should emit the structured trace from day one; this step persists + versions + replays it.

## Roleplay learnings (dizzy-0504 — sim/ manual dry-run, runs 1-3)

Entry-type vocabulary converged across runs 1-3 (see sim/sessions/contested_reservation__3.jsonl for live examples u1-u18):
- header — feat-file + scenario + level + query mode + step budget + format version.
- ruling — a Director decision on a protocol ambiguity (harness stops and asks rather than assuming; every ruling logged). Carries decision + argument_as_stated.
- injection — a scenario command entering the command queue (one at a time; run to quiescence before the next).
- activation / tool_call / query_answer / emission / finding / halt — the per-step trace.
- activation_end — closes an activation: emissions produced (possibly none) + outcome (needed the moment an activation ends without emitting).
- resolution — resolves a finding: resolves:<finding-id>, decision, argument_as_stated VERBATIM (rule 9). Categories: design-change, insufficient-context, unreviewed-component.
- branch — opens a counterfactual: parentId points at the fork node; records why and which feature-file/scenario revision applies from here.
- context — scenario givens materialized at branch start (technician-style setup the story assumes); enter the event store as pre-existing facts that queriers may cite.
- amendment (added run 3, entry u18) — run-end feat amendments applied to the artifact: applies:[ruling/resolution ids], target file, detail.
TREE SHAPE: every line {id, parentId, type, ...}. Branching = appending new entries pointing at an earlier parentId in the SAME file; context rebuild walks leaf->root. Version the format from the first commit — it becomes a de-facto public contract the moment branching exists (replay to step N, swap feature-file, resume).

## Roleplay learnings (dizzy-0504 — sim/ manual dry-run, runs 1-3)

Level-2 semantics, resolved by the roleplay (answers PLAYBOOK Q2 follow-up):
- LEVEL 2 = materialize models as CACHES OF THE STREAM. At level 0 the j->m->Q chain COLLAPSES (rule 10): projections never activate, only events are recorded, and a query is answered by a querier scanning the event store. Level 2 UN-collapses this: one JSON blob per Model lives in the session file; projections activate and propose mutations to that state THROUGH the harness; queriers answer ONLY from the supplied model state — never by scanning the raw stream.
- WHY IT MATTERS: level 2 mechanically verifies projection wiring instead of trusting a clever querier. Concrete case from run 3 (branch u): dequeue-on-hold + held-not-available. At level 0 the querier INFERRED Grace's dequeue from copy_held_for_member in the stream; at level 2 it only holds if the projections dequeue_reservation_on_hold and mark_copy_held_in_catalog actually mutate the reservations/catalog model state. Same for the unverified lend_book held-copy pickup path (get_hold_for_member answered from materialized state).
- PREREQUISITE: authored def/ schemas (the level-1 gate, dizzy-448c) so model-state shapes exist.

title: Showcase example: get_book_availability reserved-vs-held ambiguity surfaced by sim_querier
description: A perfect simulate demo finding (Director: keep as-is, do NOT fix the design). The sim_querier, asked get_book_availability with a book_reserved (Grace) in the stream, answered '0 copies' — treating a RESERVATION as reducing availability. The design says only a HOLD (copy_held_for_member) does; a reserved book with a copy on the shelf is still borrowable (hold_book: 'we do not reject reservations... the member could just borrow it'). reserved != held. Capture this run as an illustrative example of what dizzy simulate surfaces (query-description ambiguity caught with zero code). Use in docs/demo, not a code fix.

title: point/sim.py: real Session harness (session=system(session), JSONL log, resume) — level 0 working
description: DONE. Overwrote the old scaffolding with the real harness: SessionLog (append-only JSONL trace + checkpoint entries), Session (single state object: givens/event_store/evt_queue/cmd_queue/pending_cmds/step/budget/findings/exec_counts/cursor), system(session) one-advance phased drain wired to agent.py (sim executor + inline jmQ querier). load runs from scratch; resume deserializes the last checkpoint and continues the same loop (no replay-reconstruction). Context givens reach all activations (ruling c2). Verified: catalog_one (cheap loop + mid-run resume) and full borrow_available_book (3 steps, mints Ada, inline querier with answered/finding/null outcomes, findings surfaced, no speculative emit). Entry types match PLAN session-format spec. Remaining for full matrix: lib executor/emitter/querier dials, projections/ModelStore (level 2), branching.

title: point/sim.py wrapper-agent control: first-execution gate (print+quit) + load-continues + gate CLI
description: DONE. Per Director: sim.py is a stepper an outer claude/pi agent drives, not an autonomous Director. (1) load now CONTINUES an existing session instead of overwriting — crash/gate resumable by re-running the same command (note 1). (2) Rule-11 first-execution gate: before activating a never-simulated procedure/policy, sim.py records a gate entry, checkpoints, prints STATUS: GATE + verbatim description + instructions, exits 10. (3) gate CLI: 'sim.py gate <session> <component> --confirm|--modified "note"' records a ruling and marks the component reviewed; only --confirm auto-proceeds; --modified expects the human edited the feat first. (4) system() now advances one activation per step (policy_queue) for finest gate/crash granularity. Driving protocol in point/DRIVING.md. Verified gate->confirm->continue->halt as one threaded session file. Findings surfaced at HALT (not mid-run pause) for the wrapper to resolve.

title: sim.py: gate-aware step protocol — StepResult signals clean|gate|quiescent so caller halts and resumes
description: Replace the fully-automated step()/run_scenario() loop with a step model that returns a StepResult on every call. StepResult carries an outcome enum: clean (activation completed, no gate), gate_pre_activation (component has never run — halt before executing), gate_first_output (component just ran for the first time — halt before committing activation_end), quiescent (nothing left to process), and halt (step budget exhausted or livelock). The caller — whether a test script, a Claude runner, or an interactive CLI — decides what to do next: advance, review, amend, branch. This replaces the while-not-quiescent loop in run_scenario; the loop becomes the caller's responsibility. StepResult should carry enough context for the caller to act: the component name, the activation id, the gate type, and the pending tool calls / emissions if applicable.

title: sim.py: pre-first-execution description review gate
description: Before activating a component (policy or procedure) that has zero executions recorded in the current session, return gate_pre_activation from step() instead of running the executor. Execution count is derived from the session log: count policy_started/procedure_started entries whose log.procedure matches the component name. The StepResult carries the component name and its description (verbatim from the feat file) so the caller can display it for Director review. The caller then either confirms (calls step() again with the gate cleared) or amends (updates the feat file and calls step() again). If the description is amended, the caller is responsible for logging a branch. Depends on dizzy-ea81 (gate-aware step protocol).

title: sim.py: first-output review gate + activation_end entry type
description: Add activation_end as a session log entry type that closes an activation. Fields: activation_id (the policy_started/procedure_started entry it closes), outcome (clean | finding | null), and a summary of emissions produced. For a component's first execution, after the executor runs and tool calls are logged, return gate_first_output from step() instead of immediately committing activation_end. The StepResult carries the activation id and the full tool_calls list so the caller can display them for Director review. The caller approves (step() commits activation_end with outcome=clean) or reports a finding (step() logs the finding entry, commits activation_end with outcome=finding, and returns so the caller can classify the finding). For all subsequent executions, activation_end is committed automatically after tool calls are logged. Depends on dizzy-ea81 (gate-aware step protocol).

title: sim.py: finding resolution classification and deterministic branch point
description: Extend resolve() with a required category field that classifies what must change after a finding is resolved. Three categories, each with a deterministic branch point: description-change (component prose description is wrong — branch from the node before the activation started, i.e. the entry immediately before the policy_started/procedure_started that produced the finding); wiring-change (declared queries/emits/commands are wrong — same branch point as description-change); scenario-change (scenario context or commands are under-specified — branch from the injection entry where the triggering command entered the queue). resolve() should return the correct branch_from_id for the caller to use when calling branch(). The branch() call should carry resolution_id in its meta so the session log is traceable. Depends on dizzy-4993 (activation_end, which shapes what nodes exist to branch from).

title: Single-threaded phased-queue runtime: generated libraries run on the defined sequential semantics
description:
v1 spine. Generated libraries ship a single-threaded runtime: a phased queue loop (drain the event queue, then drain the command queue, repeat) — Dizzy's *defined* semantics: one legal interleaving, sequentially consistent. The chosen example must actually RUN on this, not just generate. Everything downstream (simulate scheduler, future distributed runtime, TLA+) stays consistent with these semantics. Distinct from the simulate scheduler (dizzy-3c9e), which models the feat abstractly with scripted executors; this is the real engine the generated handlers + event store execute under.

STATUS UPDATE (2026-08-18, dizzy-eea5): the runtime now EXISTS and the semantics are implemented and asserted, split across two components exactly as this seed describes. dizzy.engine.loop.Engine.run_command runs the procedure, whose emits land in a local FIFO event queue; _drain_events drains it to empty (append to store -> fold projections -> commit -> policies), and a policy's dispatched command never runs inline — it goes to the OUTER command queue and becomes the next unit of work. The second phase is therefore owned by the SCHEDULING SHELL, not by an inner loop, which means the shell is part of the defined semantics — worth stating in anything that models them (the simulate scheduler, a future TLA+ spec).

Read this seed as specifying ST, not mp. dizzy.engine.st (one lane, one process) satisfies sequential consistency; dizzy.engine.mp deliberately does not (N workers drain concurrently under at-least-once delivery, with confluent projections absorbing the reordering and duplicates). dizzy/tests/engine/test_conformance.py is now the contract and asserts BOTH halves per shell: that the uniform-queue scheduler converges to the same read models, and that it does NOT promise an identical stream — so no future change can quietly promote mp's guarantee or demote st's.

WHAT REMAINS for this seed: 'generated libraries SHIP the runtime'. Today a host hand-writes the wiring that binds the feature to the engine and hand-drives the command-queue drain (see examples/recipes/kitchen.py's run_to_quiescence). Generating that is dizzy-07fb; declaring the runtime dependency in the generated workspace is dizzy-556f.

title: FastAPI example UI: the seam proving UIs are ordinary code talking to a Dizzy library
description: v1. Deliberately boring FastAPI app that calls commands and queries against the generated library. Its only job: show Dizzy is the engine and the UI is ordinary code talking to it. Small, not impressive. Proves UIs are NOT built with Dizzy.

Broader than dizzy-7e6d, the simulate-only walkthrough.

If only happy path, add the one change — a narrative addition, not a rewrite.

Depends on TS/Rust generation (dizzy-9913) and event-schema evolution checks (dizzy compat, dizzy-9e5e).

Cross-language runtime (mixing language contexts in one runtime) IS distributed execution and lands here too.

Built in THIS repo; only the graph-rendering/visualization front-end may live elsewhere.

title: Align onboard/prime verbs with Seeds: rename dizzy onboard→prime, add onboard installer
description:
## Problem
`dizzy onboard` is misnamed. Comparing the three verbs:

| Verb | Behavior | Mutates files? | Cadence |
|------|----------|----------------|---------|
| `sd onboard` | Writes/updates a Seeds section into CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md (`--check`, `--stdout`) | YES — installer | Once per repo |
| `sd prime` | Prints agent context (rules, command ref, workflow) to stdout | No | Every session / after compaction |
| `dizzy onboard` | Prints an agent overview to stdout (components, feature-file role, change taxonomy, exemplars) | No | Read-first per session |

`dizzy onboard` is read-only and per-session — its own doc (docs/onboard.md, docs/cli.md:94-101) even says "Modeled on the seeds tool's `prime` verb." So it semantically IS `dizzy prime` wearing the wrong name. DIZZY currently has NO equivalent of `sd onboard` (the installer that injects a section into CLAUDE.md).

## Recommendation — adopt the Seeds two-verb split
1. Rename `dizzy onboard` → `dizzy prime` — the per-session context printer (it already is this).
2. Reclaim `dizzy onboard` for the installer role it's missing: write a DIZZY section into CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md (with `--check`/`--stdout`), like `sd onboard`.

Result: same mental model agents already learn from Seeds — `onboard` = install once, `prime` = load each session.

## Implementation notes / order (per CLAUDE.md conventions)
- `onboard` is a SHIPPED command (docs/cli.md:25). Change scope in docs/cli.md FIRST, then seeds, then code.
- Rename canonical doc dizzy/src/dizzy/docs/onboard.md → prime.md and update the `_print_doc("onboard.md")` call (cli.py:398-401).
- Keep a deprecation alias `onboard` → `prime` for a release for anything referencing the old name.
- New `dizzy onboard` installer: write DIZZY section to CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, support `--check` and `--stdout`.

## Minimal fallback
If renaming a shipped verb is too much churn now: just ADD `dizzy onboard` (installer) alongside the existing printer, and rename the printer to `prime` later. Downside: leaves the confusing semantics in place.

title: Generate a wiring registry in gen_int (feat topology as data)
description: Hosts currently hand-mirror the feat topology (command→procedure, event→projections/policies, procedure→queries) in wiring code and guard it with a runtime validate-against-feat check (see dizzy-logger host/wiring.py). gen_int already knows the full topology — emitting it as a generated registry (name→class maps + edges) would eliminate the duplication and the drift risk.

title: Projection context should carry the event envelope (seq, ingested_at)
description: Projections that materialize stream metadata (e.g. a timeline's ingested_at = stream-append time) have no sanctioned way to receive it: events don't carry it and the generated projection context only has the adapter. dizzy-logger works around it by subclassing SqlaAdapter with an ingested_at field set by the engine per envelope, and projections getattr() it with an occurred_at fallback. Proposal: generated projection contexts include the envelope (seq, ingested_at) alongside the event.

title: Reusable rebuild tool: (feat file, lib, connection) -> rebuilt read models
description:
SUPERSEDED IN PART by dizzy-eea5 (2026-08-18): the reusable seam now exists as dizzy.engine.rebuild.rebuild(store, session, runners, metadatas) — no ORM import, runners/metadatas injected, retired event types skipped rather than fatal — plus dizzy.engine.sqla (behind the [sqla] extra) for the SQLite cache-management half: make_engine, schema_fingerprint, and ensure_current, which heals schema drift by REBUILD rather than ALTER and judges freshness by a completion marker under a file lock. Engine.projection_runners() supplies the runners argument straight from the live wiring, so a rebuild cannot fold a different set of projections than the engine does (asserted in tests/engine/test_conformance.py).

WHAT REMAINS is only the CLI wrapper this seed asked for: a 'dizzy rebuild' verb taking (feat file, lib, connection data) that resolves the projection runners from the generated library and performs rebuild + replay-check. Blocked in practice on dizzy-07fb — resolving 'the projections registered for each event type' from a feat + lib IS the wiring generator; without it the verb would have to reimplement that resolution by reflection.

title: Convention: engine owns the read-model transaction boundary — projections never commit
description: Found while building dizzy-logger's multiprocessing engine (docs/multiprocessing-engine-strategy.md, fold-placement note). The recipes example's projection implementations call context.adapter.session.commit() inside their folds. That puts a transaction opinion in element code: the shared session gets committed N times mid-drain, an event folding through two projections can be half-committed on crash, and a different engine cannot choose a different boundary. dizzy-logger moved the commit into the engine: Engine takes commit=session.commit and commits once per event, AFTER that event's projections fold and BEFORE its policies dispatch (the pre-policy commit is what makes fold-then-enqueue hold across worker processes — a dispatched command's claimant only sees committed state). Upstream work: (1) strip session.commit() from the recipes example projections and give its engine the same per-event commit hook; (2) state the house rule wherever element authors read conventions: projections write through the adapter, never commit; the engine owns read-model transaction boundaries. Related: the reusable rebuild tool (dizzy-2cdc) becomes a single transaction under this rule.

title: Runtime kit: adopt dizzy-logger's engine/store/tooling as DIZZY-owned runtime (post-mp-soak)
description: Decision with Conrad (2026-07-09): DIZZY grows from generator to generator + runtime kit, adopting dizzy-logger's host layer once the mp engine has soaked. What moves (all already parameterized so their only feature knowledge arrives via arguments): dagstore/ (the content-addressed event DAG, standalone already); host/engine.py (control loop; owns the per-event read-model commit boundary — commit= constructor arg, see dizzy-be73); host/store.py EventStore (takes event_classes=; the gen_def-derived default map stays behind as app glue); host/rebuild.py (runners=/metadatas= injectable — supersedes/absorbs dizzy-2cdc); host/replicate.py (fold_envelopes takes runners=/reconstruct=); host/preflight.py (constraints.yaml stays app-side as data). Later phases: engines/st + engines/mp scheduling shells as extras (dizzy[st], dizzy[mp] — keep dramatiq/redis out of core deps); the conformance suite (tests/test_conformance.py) moves up as THE engine contract, running against a DIZZY-owned fixture app (recipes example) so it lives in DIZZY CI; recipes example switches to the canonical engine (closes dizzy-be73 properly). Stays app-side forever: feat file, element implementations, wiring.py (the feature binding — though generating wiring from the feat is the natural follow-on feature), env hydration, server/cli/UI. Sequencing per dizzy-logger docs/multiprocessing-engine-strategy.md: soak DIZZY_ENGINE=mp locally first — extraction wants a design that has stopped moving; the in-place parameterization is already done and green in dizzy-logger.

title: First-class simulation fold: replay drafts through registered projections into a scratch session
description: The dizzy-logger ERP feature needed a projected world: confirmed models plus events that WOULD be emitted, folded through the real projections into an in-memory session. Implemented by hand as lib/python-uv/erpfold.py: clone model tables to scratch sqlite, apply projection elements per event. DIZZY should offer this generically — fold event_list into a scratch session driven by the declared projection topology — so scenario/what-if/candidate views never require a hand-mirrored event-to-projection map. Same capability the dag-planner demo calls ScenarioEventDrafted plus scratch replay.

title: Document schema-only models with empty adapters as a supported pattern
description: A feat model with adapters: [] generates pydantic classes and no persistence — right for interchange/contract shapes. dizzy-logger uses it for erp_candidates, the proposer-settlement candidate schema. Works today because code paths use adapters-or-empty, but undocumented and untested upstream. Document and add a test so it does not regress.

title: Generated per-domain projection registry mapping events to projection elements
description: wiring.py hand-mirrors the feat topology, already flagged. The new erpfold.py had to mirror the ERP slice AGAIN to fold drafts outside the engine. Generating a registry module from the feat would eliminate both mirrors. dizzy-logger guards drift with test_erp_parity.py test_fold_topology_matches_feat, which a generated registry would make unnecessary.

title: Runtime kit phase 2: extract the engine, store and rebuild/replicate tooling into DIZZY
description:
Phase 1 (f2ffbf7, branch engine-kit) brought the engine LAYER up — dizzy.engine.registry (FeatGraph), dizzy.engine.ports (HostApp/ShellServices/Runtime), and both scheduling shells (st, mp). It left an asymmetry: dizzy.engine.mp calls runtime.engine.run_command(...) and clears runtime.engine._events, but there is no Engine class in dizzy/src at all. DIZZY owns the shells that schedule an engine it does not own. Until this lands, dizzy.engine can only run an app that brings its own engine object shaped like dizzy-logger's — which is exactly one app.

What moves (all already parameterized downstream, per the original ffdc plan): host/engine.py (the control loop: command -> procedure -> events -> projections -> policies -> commands; owns the per-event read-model commit boundary via commit=, see dizzy-be73); host/store.py EventStore (takes event_classes=, and FeatGraph.events now supplies that map from the feat instead of a module scan); dagstore/ (the content-addressed event DAG — standalone already, zero runtime deps); host/rebuild.py (runners=/metadatas= injectable; supersedes/absorbs dizzy-2cdc); host/replicate.py (fold_envelopes takes runners=/reconstruct=). Stays app-side: constraints.yaml and preflight (app data), env hydration, server/CLI/UI.

Packaging is already prepared: phase 1 split dizzy's deps so core is pyyaml only, with the generator behind [gen] and the mp broker behind [mp]. The engine needs a read-model adapter, so decide whether sqlalchemy lands in core or behind a [sqla] extra — a worker that only schedules should not be forced to carry an ORM.

Two things to finish alongside it: (1) move tests/test_conformance.py up as THE engine contract and run it against a DIZZY-owned fixture app, which means switching examples/recipes onto the canonical engine and closing dizzy-be73 properly — today recipes does not touch dizzy.engine at all, so the shells have no in-repo app exercising them; (2) this is a prerequisite for the wiring generator, because the Engine is what encodes the ordering rule (projections fold before policies dispatch) that a hand-written wiring otherwise has to restate per event.

Relationship to dizzy-29aa (the v1 phased-queue runtime / defined semantics), checked 2026-08-18: dizzy-logger's Engine ALREADY implements those semantics, split across two components. run_command runs the procedure, whose emits land in a local FIFO event queue; _drain_events drains that queue to empty (append to store -> fold projections -> commit -> policies), and a policy's dispatched command never runs inline — it goes to the OUTER command queue and becomes the next unit of work. That is 'drain the event queue, then drain the command queue, repeat', with the second phase owned by the scheduling shell rather than by an inner loop. Worth stating explicitly when extracting, because it means the SHELL IS PART OF THE DEFINED SEMANTICS — which matters to anything modelling them (the simulate scheduler, a future TLA+ spec).

One real divergence to record now rather than discover later: 29aa specifies ONE legal interleaving, sequentially consistent. The st shell (single lane) satisfies that. The MP SHELL DELIBERATELY DOES NOT — N worker processes drain the command queue concurrently under at-least-once delivery, and the confluent projections absorb the duplicates and the reordering. So DIZZY now ships one conforming runtime and one deliberately weaker one. The conformance suite this seed moves up should assert WHICH semantics each shell claims rather than assuming both claim the same, and dizzy-29aa should be read as specifying st, not mp.

title: Generate wiring.py from the feat file — the last hand-mirrored artifact
description:
Decision with Conrad (2026-08-18): GENERATED, not runtime-reflective. A runtime binder was considered and rejected on start-up cost — every process would pay module resolution before serving. Generated wiring is also greppable, diffable when a feat changes, and debuggable in a stack trace. Runtime binding keeps some appeal (zero generated surface, no regeneration step) and is worth revisiting later, but it is explicitly NOT the priority.

The gap this closes: dizzy generate turns a feat into schemas, contracts and element stubs, and dizzy.engine can now schedule them — but every app must still hand-write the binding between the two. dizzy-logger's host/wiring.py is 1518 lines of it; examples/recipes/kitchen.py is 330 more.

Evidence that it is a pure function of the feat. The feat declares, per element, exactly the argument list of the generated context constructor: a procedure's command: -> register_procedure(<CommandClass>, ...); its emits: -> emit=<proc>_emitters(<event>=eng.emit_event); its queries: -> query=<proc>_queries(<q>=<bound query>); its environment: -> env=<proc>_env(<shape>=env.<shape>); its telemetry: -> telemetry=<proc>_telemetry(<sink>=telemetry.<sink>). A projection's event:/model:/adapter: give the event->projection routing; a policy's event:/emits: give its registration and dispatch targets. All 1518 lines are that one template repeated.

Only three exceptions exist in the real app, and none is a counterexample. (1) Lazy imports for capability-pool elements (detect_faces, embed_image, embed_text) so a node without the ml extra never imports them — driven by constraints.yaml, not the feat, and correctly outside a feat-driven generator. (2) _fresh_turn_stop — a query that must run on a short-lived session to observe other writers. (3) _turn_queries, which fills a generated queries dataclass BY REFLECTION with the stated goal 'a new feat query becomes tool-visible with no wiring edit' — someone already reached for generation inside the hand-written file. So the generator needs one declared escape hatch: an app may override any element's runner by name, and the generated module must make that a supported seam rather than a fork.

Shape: emit engine-mediated wiring, not the direct element-to-element style kitchen.py uses (where a policy is called inline and a dispatched command recurses straight back into a procedure). Engine-mediated is what the shells expect, and it lets the Engine own the ordering rule — projections fold before policies dispatch — instead of each generated event handler restating it. Output should also produce the HostApp/build_runtime that dizzy.engine.ports expects, so 'generate + implement the bodies + run' has no hand-written glue left.

Blocked by dizzy-eea5 (phase 2): the Engine has to be DIZZY's before the generated wiring can target it. Subsumes dizzy-659b (generated event->projection registry), which is one slice of this output; dizzy-logger's test_erp_parity.py fold-topology guard and host/wiring.py's own validate_against_feat both become unnecessary once the wiring cannot drift from the feat by construction.

title: Generated python-uv workspace should declare the DIZZY runtime dependency
description:
Discovered while switching examples/recipes onto the canonical engine (dizzy-eea5, 2026-08-18). A host built on the runtime kit imports dizzy.engine, but the generated lib/python-uv/pyproject.toml is only a [tool.uv.workspace] member list — it declares no dependencies at all. So running any generated library's host needs the runtime layered in by hand: 'uv run --project <lib> --with-editable . python demo.py' (or --with dizzy outside the repo), which is what examples/recipes/README.md now documents.

That works, but it means 'dizzy generate libraries' emits a workspace that cannot run its own feature without an undocumented extra flag. Options: (a) give the generated workspace root a [project] table depending on dizzy, (b) add dizzy to each element package's deps (wrong — elements import gen_def/gen_int, not the engine; only the HOST needs it), or (c) emit the dependency only alongside generated wiring, since that is the artifact that actually imports dizzy.engine. (c) pairs naturally with dizzy-07fb: the generated wiring and its dependency declaration are the same deliverable. Note that changing the generated workspace pyproject touches generator snapshots and 'just examples-check'.
